paragraphs: Axcelis Technologies, Inc. ("Axcelis," the "Company," "we," "us," or "our") designs, manufactures and services ion implantation and other processing equipment used in the fabrication of semiconductor chips. We believe that our Purion family of products offers the most innovative implanters available on the market today. We sell to leading semiconductor chip manufacturers worldwide. The ion implantation business represented 98.2% of our revenue in 2025, with the remaining 1.8% of revenue derived from aftermarket sales associated with other legacy processing systems. In addition to equipment, we provide extensive aftermarket lifecycle products and services, including used tools, spare parts, equipment upgrades, maintenance services and customer training.

Axcelis' business commenced in 1978 and its current corporate entity was incorporated in Delaware in 1995. We are headquartered in Beverly, Massachusetts and maintain an internet site at www.axcelis.com. On or through our website, investors may access, free of charge, our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, and amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act") as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file such material with, or furnish it to, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). Our website and the information contained therein or connected thereto shall not be deemed to be incorporated into this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Revenue for 2025 was $839.0 million, compared to $1,017.9 million in 2024. Systems revenue for 2025 was $571.0 million, compared to $782.6 million in 2024. Gross margin percent for 2025 was 44.9% compared to 44.7% in 2024. Operating profit for 2025 was $119.3 million, compared to $210.8 million in 2024. Net income for 2025 was $120.2 million, compared to $201.0 million in 2024.

The Company is in a strong competitive position. A focused strategy on ion implant, combined with the hard work and dedication of our employees and the support of our customers and suppliers, enabled us to achieve critical milestones in our drive to market leadership. Important accomplishments in 2025 included:
● We delivered revenue of $839.0 million in 2025 and earnings per share of $3.80.
● We remained a technology leader and supplier of choice in the implant-intensive power device segment, which accounted for 55% of the value of our 2025 system shipments.
● We continued working to expand our footprint with existing and new customers and currently have four Purion evaluation systems in the field at strategic customer sites in key market segments.

● We continued our investment in our Customer Solutions & Innovation ("CS&I") aftermarket business to drive financial growth and increased customer satisfaction levels, including the "Digital Tool Box," an innovative service offering with online training, remote diagnosis and install, and automated troubleshooting guide.

● We received 16 customer satisfaction awards in 2025. In addition, Axcelis was named to the 2024 editions of Forbes' List of America's Best Mid-Cap Companies and to Fortune Magazine's 2024 lists of the Top 100 Fastest Growing Companies.

We continue to work diligently to ensure that manufacturing and operating expense levels remain well aligned to business conditions. We believe that the most fundamental interest of our stockholders is consistent, profitable financial performance, which we expect to continue to deliver in 2026. Our performance is subject to the risks and uncertainties discussed below under Item 1A, Risk Factors.

Semiconductor chips, also known as integrated circuits, are used in a continuously evolving range of consumer and industrial products, including for example, personal computers, mobile devices, automobiles, sensors and controllers for the "internet of things" and data storage servers. Types of semiconductor chips include dynamic random-access memory

("DRAM") and "Not AND" ("NAND") Flash memory; logic devices to process information; and "system on chip" devices (which have both logic and memory features). The demand for chips continues to increase, as a result of the electrification of vehicles, the evolution of digital communications (including the introduction of 5G mobile networks), artificial intelligence, large language models (e.g. ChatGPT), data analytics and visualization, and the growth in the Internet of Things, and the increasing complexity of device features. These chips are used in power management, data input, such as image sensors, which are often manufactured using mature processing technologies, as well as for memory to support the storage of data, internet streaming and "cloud computing" data analytics.

Most semiconductor chips are built on silicon or silicon carbide ("SiC") wafers of 150mm (6 inches), 200mm (8 inches) or 300mm (12 inches) in diameter. Each semiconductor chip is made up of millions of tiny transistors or "switches" to control the functions of the device. Transistors are created in the wafer by introducing various precisely placed dopants into the silicon or SiC in specific patterns.

Semiconductor chip manufacturers own or manage wafer fabrication facilities (often referred to as "fabs"), which utilize many different types of equipment in the making of integrated circuits. Over 300 process steps utilizing over 50 different types of process tools are required to make a single device like a microprocessor. Semiconductor chip manufacturers seek device performance benefits through new products and technology enhancements and productivity improvements through increased throughput, equipment utilization and higher manufacturing yields. Capacity is added by increasing the amount of manufacturing equipment in existing fabrication facilities and by constructing new fabrication facilities.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
If semiconductor chip manufacturers do not make sufficient capital expenditures, our sales and profitability will be harmed.
If we fail to develop and introduce reliable new or enhanced products and services that meet the needs of semiconductor chip manufacturers, our results will suffer.
Axcelis is subject to the risks of operating internationally: we derive a substantial portion of our revenue from outside the United States, especially from Asia.
The impact of tariffs on our business is difficult to predict, and may change substantially and without notice.
Our dependence upon suppliers for many components and sub-assemblies could result in increased costs or delays in the manufacture and sale of our products.
A significant portion of our revenue depends on customers electing to buy aftermarket products and services from Axcelis.
If we fail to compete successfully in the highly competitive semiconductor capital equipment industry, our sales and profitability will decline.
We are dependent on sales to a limited number of large customers; the loss of a significant customer or any reduction in orders from them could materially affect our sales.
Our international operations involve currency risk.
We may not be able to maintain and expand our business if we are not able to hire, retain and integrate qualified personnel.
Our financial results may fluctuate significantly.
Our financial results may fall short of anticipated levels because forecasting revenue and profitability is complex and may be inaccurate.
Axcelis is exposed to risks related to cybersecurity threats and incidents.
Axcelis is subject to risks associated with compliance with environmental, health and safety regulations.
Our financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected by global pandemics.
Our proprietary technology may be vulnerable to efforts by competitors to challenge or design around, potentially reducing our market share.
If operations were to be disrupted at Axcelis' manufacturing facilities, it would have a negative impact on our business.
If we do not have access to capital on favorable terms, on the timeline we anticipate, or at all, our financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.
The market price of our common stock may be volatile, which could result in substantial losses for investors.
We operate in jurisdictions with complex and changing tax laws.
Risks Related to the Merger
The exchange ratio is fixed and will not be adjusted in the event of any change in either Axcelis' or Veeco's stock price.
The Merger may be delayed or may not be completed and the Merger Agreement may be terminated in accordance with its terms, which could materially and adversely effect Axcelis and/or Veeco.
Regulatory approvals may not be received, may take longer than expected or may impose conditions that are not presently anticipated or that cannot be met.

Axcelis stockholders and Veeco stockholders will each have reduced ownership and voting interest in the combined company as compared to ownership and voting interest in each of Axcelis and Veeco on a standalone basis.

The Merger Agreement may prevent Axcelis and Veeco from entering into certain transactions and taking certain actions that might otherwise be beneficial to Axcelis or Veeco and their respective stockholders
Litigation against Axcelis and Veeco could prevent or delay the completion of the Merger or result in the payment of damages following completion of the Merger.
Failure to attract, motivate and retain executives and other key employees could diminish the anticipated benefits of the Merger.
Each of Axcelis and Veeco will incur significant transaction, merger-related and restructuring costs in connection with the Merger.
Axcelis stockholders and Veeco stockholders will not be entitled to appraisal rights in the Merger.
paragraphs: Set forth below and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and in other documents we file with the SEC are risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. It is not possible to predict or identify all such risk factors. Consequently, the following is not a complete discussion of all potential risks or uncertainties.

New systems orders and used tool sales depend upon demand from semiconductor chip manufacturers who build or expand fabrication facilities. When the rate of construction or expansion of fabrication facilities declines, demand for our systems will decline, reducing our revenue. In addition, all or a portion of the demand for increased capacity may be satisfied by a semiconductor chip manufacturer's ability to reconfigure and re-use equipment they already own. Revenue decline also hurts our profitability because our established cost structure and our continued investments in engineering, research and development, and marketing necessary to develop new products and to maintain extensive customer service and support capabilities, limit our ability to reduce expenses in proportion to declining sales.

Rapid technological changes in semiconductor chip manufacturing processes require us to respond quickly to changing customer requirements. Our future success will depend in part upon our ability to develop, manufacture and successfully introduce new systems and product lines with improved capabilities. This will depend upon a variety of factors, including new product selection, timely and efficient completion of product design and development as well as manufacturing and assembly processes, product performance in the field and effective sales and marketing. In particular:

● We must continue to develop competitive technical specifications for new systems, or enhancements to our existing systems, and manufacture and ship these systems or enhancements in volume in a timely manner.

● We will need to accurately predict the schedule on which our customers will be ready to transition to new products, in order to accurately forecast demand for new products while managing the transition from older products.

● We will need to effectively manage product reliability or quality problems that often exist with new systems, in order to avoid higher manufacturing costs, delays in acceptance and payment and additional service and warranty expenses, and ultimately, a lack of repeat orders.

paragraphs: Certain statements in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" are forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. The semiconductor capital equipment industry is subject to cyclical swings in capital spending by semiconductor chip manufacturers. Capital spending is influenced by demand for semiconductors and the products using them, the utilization rate and capacity of existing semiconductor chip manufacturing facilities and changes in semiconductor technology, all of which are outside of our control. As a result, our revenue may fluctuate from year to year and period to period. Our established cost structure does not vary significantly with changes in volume. We may also experience fluctuations in operating results and cash flows depending on our revenue level.

Revenue for 2025 was $839.0 million, compared to $1,017.9 million in 2024. Systems revenue for 2025 was $571.0 million, compared to $782.6 million in 2024. Gross margin percent for the year was 44.9% compared to 44.7% in 2024. Operating profit was $119.3 million in 2025, compared to $210.8 million in 2024. Net income for the year was $120.2 million, compared to $201.0 million in 2024.

The Company is in a strong competitive position. A focused strategy on ion implant, combined with the hard work and dedication of our employees and the encouragement and support of our customers and suppliers, enabled us to achieve numerous critical milestones in our drive to market leadership. Important accomplishments in 2025 included:
● We delivered revenue of $839.0 million in 2025 and earnings per share of $3.80.
● We remained a technology leader and supplier of choice in the implant-intensive power device segment, which accounted for 55% of the value of our 2025 system shipments.
● We continued working to expand our footprint with existing and new customers and currently have four Purion evaluation systems in the field at strategic customer sites in key market segments.

● We continued our investment in our Customer Solutions & Innovation ("CS&I") aftermarket business to drive financial growth and increased customer satisfaction levels, including the "Digital Tool Box," an innovative service offering with online training, remote diagnosis and install, and automated troubleshooting guide.

● We received 16 customer satisfaction awards in 2025. In addition, Axcelis was named to the 2024 editions of Forbes' List of America's Best Mid-Cap Companies and to Fortune Magazine's 2024 lists of the Top 100 Fastest Growing Companies.
We continue to work diligently to ensure that manufacturing and operating expense levels remain well aligned to business conditions.

The market for our systems and aftermarket products and services is represented by a relatively small number of companies. In 2025, the top 20 semiconductor chip manufacturers accounted for approximately 86.4% of total semiconductor capital equipment spending, down from 87.6% in 2024. Our net revenue from our ten largest customers accounted for 55.2% of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 45.9% and 51.7% of revenue for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively. For the year ended December 31, 2025, one customer represented 11.0% percent of total revenue.

Management's discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations are based upon Axcelis' consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States. The preparation of these financial statements requires management to make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses, and related disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities. On an on-going basis, we evaluate our estimates and assumptions. Management's estimates are based on historical experience and on various other assumptions that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources. Actual results may differ from these estimates under different assumptions or conditions.

We believe the following accounting policies are critical in the portrayal of our financial condition and results of operations and require management's most significant judgments and estimates in the preparation of our consolidated financial statements. For additional accounting policies, see Note 2 to the consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025 included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Our accounting policies relating to the recognition of revenue require management to make estimates, determinations and judgments based on historical experience and on various other assumptions, which include (i) the existence of a contract with the customer, (ii) the identification of the performance obligations in the contract, (iii) the value of any variable consideration in the contract, (iv) the standalone selling price of multiple obligations in the contract, for the purpose of allocating the consideration in the contract, and (v) determining when a performance obligation has been met. Our revenue recognition policies are set forth in section (k) of Note 2, Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, to the consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025 included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Recognition of revenue based on incorrect judgments, including an erroneous allocation of the estimated sales price between the units of accounting, could result in inappropriate recognition of revenue, or incorrect timing of revenue recognition, which could have a material effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

paragraphs: Axcelis Technologies, Inc. ("Axcelis," the "Company," "we," "us," or "our") 研發、製造與維修用於半導體晶片製造的離子植入與其他處理設備。我們認為，我們的 Purion 系列產品提供目前市場上最具創新性的植入設備。我們銷售給全球領先的半導體晶片製造商。離子植入業務在 2025 年佔本公司營業收入的 98.2%，其餘 1.8% 的營業收入來自於其他遺留處理系統的後市場銷售。除了設備，我們也提供廣泛的後市場生命週期產品與服務，包括二手設備、備用零組件、設備升級、維護服務與客戶培訓。

Axcelis 的業務自 1978 年開始，目前的公司實體於 1995 年在特拉華州註冊成立。本公司總部設於馬薩諸塞州貝弗利，並維護一個網站於 www.axcelis.com。透過或於本公司網站上，投資人可免費取得本公司依照 10-K 表格所提交的年度報告、依照 10-Q 表格所提交的季度報告、依照 8-K 表格所提交的現況報告，以及這些報告的修正版本，這些報告或資料係依照 1934 年證券交易法第 13(a) 或 15(d) 節（經修正）所規定，於本公司電子提交至美國證券交易委員會（"SEC"）或提供給該委員會後儘速取得。本公司網站及其網站上所載資訊或與該網站相關之資訊，不應被視為本年度 10-K 表格報告之組成部分。

2025 年營業收入為 839.0 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 1,017.9 百萬美元相比。2025 年系統收入為 571.0 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 782.6 百萬美元相比。2025 年毛利率為 44.9%，與 2024 年的 44.7% 相比。2025 年營運獲利為 119.3 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 210.8 百萬美元相比。2025 年淨利為 120.2 百萬美元，與 2024 年的 201.0 百萬美元相比。
本公司處於強勁的競爭地位。專注於離子植入的策略，加上員工的努力與奉獻，以及客戶與供應商的支持，使我們在朝向市場領導地位的過程中達成關鍵里程碑。2025 年的重要成績包括：
● 我們在 2025 年實現了 839.0 百萬美元的營業收入，每股盈餘為 3.80 美元。
● 我們持續在植入密集型功率裝置領域保持技術領導地位與首選供應商地位，該領域佔我們 2025 年系統出貨價值的 55%。
● 我們持續努力擴大與現有與新客戶的合作，目前在關鍵市場領域的戰略客戶現場有四臺 Purion 評估系統。
● 我們持續投資於客戶解決方案與創新（"CS&I"）後市場業務，以推動財務成長與提高客戶滿意度，包括 "數位工具箱"，這是一項創新服務，提供線上培訓、遠端診斷與安裝，以及自動化故障排除指南。
● 我們在 2025 年獲得了 16 項客戶滿意度獎項。此外，Axcelis 被列入 2024 年福布斯雜誌的美國中型成長企業名單，以及列入《財富》雜誌 2024 年度 Top 100 最快成長公司名單。
我們持續努力確保製造與營運費用水平與業務狀況保持良好配合。我們認為本公司股東最基本的共同利益是持續且獲利的財務表現，我們預期在 2026 年持續提供。本公司表現受到下文 Item 1A 項風險因素所討論的風險與不確定性影響。
半導體晶片，亦稱為積體電路，被用於持續進化的消費者與工業產品範圍，包括例如個人電腦、行動裝置、汽車、用於 "物聯網" 的感測器與控制器以及資料儲存伺服器。半導體晶片的類型包括動態隨機存取記憶體

"DRAM" 以及 "Not AND" ("NAND") Flash 記憶體；用來處理資訊的邏輯元件；以及具備邏輯與記憶體功能的 "system on chip" 元件。由於電動車電氣化、數位通訊的演進（包括 5G 移動網路的引入）、人工智慧、大型語言模型（例如 ChatGPT）、資料分析與視覺化、以及物聯網的成長，以及裝置功能的日益複雜，對晶片的需求持續增加。這些晶片用於電源管理、資料輸入，例如影像感測器，這些感測器通常使用成熟的製程技術來製造，也用於記憶體以支援資料儲存、網路串流以及 "cloud computing" 資料分析。
大多數的半導體晶片是以矽或碳化矽（"SiC"）為基板，製造成直徑為 150mm（6 英寸）、200mm（8 英寸）或 300mm（12 英寸）的晶圓。每個半導體晶片由數百萬個微小的電晶體或 "開關" 組成，用以控制裝置的功能。電晶體是透過將各種精確放置的摻雜劑引入矽或 SiC 的特定圖案中製造出來的。
半導體晶片製造商擁有或管理晶圓製造廠（通常稱為 "fabs"），這些製造廠在製造積體電路的過程中會使用許多不同類型的設備。製造單一裝置如微處理器，需要超過 300 個製程步驟，並使用超過 50 種不同類型的製程設備。半導體晶片製造商透過新產品與技術改良來追求裝置性能的提升，並透過提高產能、設備使用率與製造良率來提升生產力。產能則透過在現有製造廠中增加製造設備數量，或建設新的製造廠來增加。

paragraphs: 「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」中某些陳述為前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。詞彙如 may、will、should、would、anticipates、expects、intends、plans、believes、seeks、estimates 及類似表達方式，用以識別此類前瞻性陳述。本文件所含之前瞻性陳述係基於目前預期，並涉及各種風險與不確定性，可能導致實際結果與該等前瞻性陳述所表達者有重大差異。導致此差異的因素包括，但不限於「流動性與資本資源」及「風險因素」所列者，以及其他於本年度報告表 10-K 其他部分討論之內容。讀者應謹慎勿過度依賴此等前瞻性陳述，此等陳述僅反映管理層截至本文件出具日之分析。本公司不負有更新此等前瞻性陳述以反映實際結果或影響前瞻性陳述之因素或假設之變化之義務，除非法律另有規定。
半導體資本設備產業受半導體晶片製造商資本支出週期性波動之影響。資本支出受半導體需求及使用半導體之產品需求、現有半導體晶片製造設施之利用率與產能，以及半導體技術變更等因素影響，而這些因素均為本公司所無法控制。因此，本公司之營業收入可能每年或每季有所波動。本公司已建立之成本結構，對銷售量變動並無顯著影響。本公司亦可能根據營業收入水準，而經驗到營運成果與現金流之波動。

2025 年營業收入為 839.0 百萬美元，較 2024 年之 1,017.9 百萬美元為低。2025 年系統營收為 571.0 百萬美元，較 2024 年之 782.6 百萬美元為低。全年毛利率為 44.9%，較 2024 年之 44.7% 稍高。2025 年營運獲利為 119.3 百萬美元，較 2024 年之 210.8 百萬美元為低。2025 年淨利為 120.2 百萬美元，較 2024 年之 201.0 百萬美元為低。
本公司處於強勢競爭地位。專注於離子植入之策略，加上員工之努力與奉獻，以及客戶與供應商之鼓勵與支持，使本公司在朝向市場領導地位的過程中達成許多關鍵里程碑。2025 年重要成績包括：
● 本公司於 2025 年實現 839.0 百萬美元營收，每股盈餘為 3.80 美元。
● 本公司持續為植入密集型功率元件領域之技術領導者與首選供應商，該領域佔本公司 2025 年系統出貨價值之 55%。
● 本公司持續與現有及新客戶合作，擴大市場佔有率，目前在關鍵市場領域之戰略客戶現場，已有四套 Purion 評估系統在運作中。
● 本公司持續投資於客戶解決方案與創新（"CS&I"）後市場業務，以推動財務成長與提高客戶滿意度，包括 "數位工具箱"，這是一項創新服務方案，提供線上培訓、遠端診斷與安裝，以及自動化故障排除指南。
● 我們在 2025 年收到 16 項客戶滿意度獎項。此外，Axcelis 被列入 2024 年福布斯雜誌「美國中型成長企業」名單，以及《財富》雜誌 2024 年「百大最快成長企業」名單。
我們持續努力確保製造與營運費用水準與業務狀況保持良好一致。

我們系統與後市場產品及服務的市場由相對少數的公司所代表。2025 年，前 20 大半導體晶片製造商佔總半導體設備支出約 86.4%，較 2024 年的 87.6% 下降。我們來自十家最大客戶的淨銷售額佔 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年總營業收入 55.2%，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年的 45.9% 和 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年的 51.7% 高。2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，單一客戶佔總營業收入 11.0%。

管理階層對我們財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析，係根據 Axcelis 合併財務報表，該財務報表係依照美國通用會計準則編製。這些財務報表的編製需要管理階層做出估計與判斷，影響資產、負債、收入與費用的報導數額，以及相關的或有資產與負債揭露。我們持續評估這些估計與假設。管理階層的估計係基於歷史經驗，以及在特定情況下認為合理的其他假設，這些假設的結果成為判斷資產與負債帳面價值的基礎，而這些價值無法從其他來源直接取得。實際結果可能因不同假設或條件而與這些估計不同。
我們認為以下會計政策對我們財務狀況與營運成果的呈現至關重要，且在編製我們合併財務報表時，需要管理階層做出最重大的判斷與估計。如需更多會計政策資訊，請參閱 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年合併財務報表的附註 2，包含於本 10-K 年度報告中。

我們關於收入認列的會計政策需要管理階層根據歷史經驗與各種其他假設做出估計、判斷與決定，包括 (i) 與客戶存在契約，(ii) 識別契約中的履行義務，(iii) 契約中任何變動考量的價值，(iv) 契約中多重義務的單獨銷售價格，用以分配契約中的考量，以及 (v) 判斷履行義務是否已達成。我們的收入認列政策請參閱 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年合併財務報表附註 2 中「重要會計政策摘要」的 (k) 項，包含於本 10-K 年度報告中。基於錯誤判斷的收入認列，包括錯誤分配預估銷售價格至各會計單位，可能導致收入認列不恰當，或收入認列時間不正確，這可能會對我們的財務狀況與營運成果產生重大影響。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關之風險
若半導體晶片製造商未進行足夠之資本支出，將會對我們之銷售及獲利造成損害。
若我們未能開發並推出可靠之新產品或增強型產品與服務，以符合半導體晶片製造商之需求，將會使我們之營運結果受損。
Axcelis 面臨國際營運之風險：我們之營業收入有相當大一部分來自美國境外，尤其是亞洲地區。
關稅對我們業務之影響難以預測，且可能大幅變動且無預警。
我們對於許多零組件及子組裝之供應商之依賴，可能導致製造與銷售我們產品之成本增加或延遲。
我們營業收入之重要部分取決於客戶選擇自 Axcelis 購買後市場產品與服務。
若我們未能在高度競爭之半導體資本設備產業中成功競爭，將導致我們之銷售及獲利下降。
本公司對少數大型客戶之銷售依賴度高；若失去重要客戶或這些客戶訂單減少，可能對本公司銷售造成重大影響。
本公司國際業務涉及貨幣風險。
若本公司無法聘僱、留任及整合合格人才，可能無法維持並擴大業務。
本公司財務結果可能出現顯著波動。
本公司財務結果可能低於預期，因預測營業收入與獲利性複雜且可能不準確。
Axcelis 面臨與網路安全威脅及事件相關之風險。
Axcelis 面臨與遵循環境、健康及安全法規相關之風險。
本公司財務狀況及營運結果可能因全球大流行病而受到不利影響。
本公司自有技術可能面臨競爭對手挑戰或繞過的風險，可能導致我們的市場佔有率下降。
若 Axcelis 的製造設施運作中斷，將對本公司業務產生負面影響。
若本公司無法在預期時間內以有利條件取得資金，或根本無法取得資金，將可能對本公司財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
本公司普通股的市場價格可能波動，這可能會導致投資人遭受重大損失。
本公司營運於稅法複雜且不斷變動的司法管轄區域。
與合併相關的風險
交換比率為固定，不會因 Axcelis 或 Veeco 股價變動而調整。
合併可能延遲或無法完成，且合併協議可能根據其條款終止，這可能會對 Axcelis 和/或 Veeco 造成重大且不利的影響。
法規審批可能無法取得，或耗時較預期更久，或設有未預期或無法達成之條件。
Axcelis 股東與 Veeco 股東在合併後之公司將持有較少之股權與投票權，較其各自獨立時之股權與投票權為低。
合併協議可能阻止 Axcelis 與 Veeco 進行某些交易或採取某些行動，這些行動可能對 Axcelis 或 Veeco 及其各自股東有利。
針對 Axcelis 與 Veeco 之訴訟可能阻止或延宕合併之完成，或在合併完成後導致賠償金之支付。
無法吸引、激勵並留住高階主管及其他關鍵員工，可能降低合併預期之效益。
Axcelis 與 Veeco 各自將因合併而產生重大之交易成本、合併相關成本及重整成本。
Axcelis 股東與 Veeco 股東在合併中將無權取得評價權。
paragraphs: 下列所列及本年度報告表10-K其他部分與本公司向SEC所提交之其他文件中，皆為可能導致實際結果與本年度報告表10-K中所含之預測性陳述所預期結果有重大差異之風險與不確定性。無法預測或識別所有此類風險因素。因此，以下並非對所有潛在風險或不確定性之完整討論。

新系統訂單與二手工具銷售取決於半導體晶片製造商建造或擴建製造設施之需求。當製造設施建造或擴建速率下降時，對本公司系統之需求將下降，進而減少本公司之營業收入。此外，半導體晶片製造商可能透過重新配置與再利用其現有設備來滿足部分或全部對增加產能之需求。營業收入下降也會影響本公司之利潤，因本公司既有的成本結構與持續投入工程、研究與開發及行銷之經費，用以開發新產品並維持廣泛之客戶服務與支援能力，使本公司難以按比例減少費用以配合銷售額之下降。
半導體晶片製造流程之快速技術變遷，要求本公司迅速回應客戶需求之變化。本公司未來之成功在部分程度上取決於本公司能否開發、製造並成功推出具改進功能之新系統與產品線。此將取決於多種因素，包括新產品選項、產品設計與開發之時程與效率、製造與組裝流程、產品在現場之表現，以及有效之銷售與行銷。特別是：
● 本公司必須持續開發具競爭力之新系統技術規格，或對現有系統之升級，並在合適時程內製造與出貨這些系統或升級產品。
● 本公司將需要準確預測客戶準備轉換至新產品之時程，以準確預測新產品之需求，同時管理從舊產品轉換之過程。
● 本公司將需要有效管理新系統之產品可靠性或品質問題，以避免提高製造成本、延遲採納與付款，以及額外之服務與保固費用，並最終導致重複訂單之缺乏。
